summary: PTC agreed to be acquired by Schneider Electric for $205 per share in cash, and the stock closed at 194.45 after a very large one-week jump. With the price already close to the cash offer, the expected move relative to the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days is small and depends mainly on regulatory and shareholder approvals. An unverified message-board claim of a second bidder is not counted.

flags.why: A definitive cash merger agreement is a material acquisition event that fixes the likely payout near the offer price but caps upside and adds closing risk.
flags.quote: will be converted into the right to receive $205 in cash, without interest

evidence_for.claim: The all-cash offer of $205 per share sits close to the last close of 194.45, leaving limited room to beat or trail the market by more than 2 points.
evidence_for.quote: All-cash acquisition at $205 per share for 100% of the share capital of PTC

evidence_against.claim: Completion depends on antitrust and foreign investment clearances, so a delay or block could move the stock away from the offer price.
evidence_against.quote: certain regulatory clearances required under antitrust and foreign investment laws, including expiration or early termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended

would_change_call: A confirmed competing offer, a regulatory block, or a termination of the merger agreement would change the call.
